answer:
Solve a small-deformation, linear-elastic torsion problem for a solid circular shaft using the N–mm–MPa unit system.
The shaft is a cantilever in torsion: fixed at x = 0 with rotation fully constrained (φ(0) = 0) and free at x = L = 1200 mm.
The cross-section is solid circular with diameter d = 30 mm, radius r = 15 mm, polar moment of inertia J = πd⁴/32 ≈ 79521.6 mm⁴, and torsional section modulus Wt = J/r ≈ 5301.4 mm³.
The material is AISI 1020 steel with shear modulus G = 76923.1 MPa.
The only loads are two external torques: T1 = +200000 N·mm applied at the free end x = L = 1200 mm (positive direction) and T2 = −200000 N·mm applied at x = a = 400 mm (opposite direction).
No transverse forces, bending loads, or distributed torques act on the shaft; "shear loading" refers only to torsional shear stress on cross-sections.
Part (a): determine the internal torque in each segment as constant values with sign — segment 1 (0 ≤ x < 400 mm) and segment 2 (400 mm < x ≤ 1200 mm) — noting that since T1 + T2 = 0, the reaction torque at the fixed end is zero and the two segments carry equal and opposite internal torques (±200000 N·mm).
Part (b): compute the maximum shear stress in each segment using τ_max = T_segment · r / J, evaluated at the outer surface r = 15 mm, reporting one signed value per segment in MPa.
Part (c): compute the total twist angle at the free end relative to the fixed end, φ(L) = T_segment1 · L1 / (G·J) + T_segment2 · L2 / (G·J), with L1 = 400 mm and L2 = 800 mm, reporting one signed value in radians indicating the direction of rotation.
Present the governing relations clearly: internal torque equilibrium per segment, τ_max = T·r/J, and φ = Σ T_i·L_i/(G·J).
State any additional assumptions needed (e.g., circular cross-section remains plane, no warping, material homogeneous and isotropic, stresses below yield).
Final answers must be the key numerical values per part with correct signs and units; continuous distribution curves along the axis are not required, though piecewise-constant expressions for T(x) may be included.
